messages:
arya: Heads-up: after rolling kernel 6.1.0-rc1 -> 6.1.4 across a small canary of eu-west2 P4 fleet, we saw 6 hosts hit recurring 'oom-kill' and GPU module unload/load churn. Noticed modprobe errors and some pods crashing with CUDA init failures.

mike: Can you paste uname + dmesg excerpt and driver info?

arya: Sure — quick run from host p4-eu-12:
```
$ uname -a
Linux p4-eu-12 6.1.4-custom #1 SMP Mon Mar 2 10:12:22 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader\530.41.03
$ dmesg | tail -n 40\[  102.345678] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[  102.346002] nvidia: Unknown symbol nv_map_pages
[  102.346100] CPU0: tasks blocked for more than 120 seconds
[  102.346800] oom-kill: kill process 9182 (python) score 896
[  102.347002] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing
```
This looks like module ABI/API mismatch on kernel 6.1 vs our built driver. Also seeing 'nvidia-modeset' fallbacks.

sam: Did DKMS rebuild logs run during the kernel update? We usually expect DKMS to recompile.

arya: DKMS log shows build succeeded but with warnings. However modprobe still fails with undefined symbols. Could be kernel API changes in 6.x that break prebuilt kernels/drivers even if DKMS reports success.

joanne: How many hosts impacted vs canary size? Impact on Dedicated capacity?

arya: Canary was 12 hosts, 6 affected with intermittent host instability and some allocated GPUs showing as 'Loss of NVLINK' and worker exits. A few production Dedicated pools had autoscale triggers due to pod restarts — cost bump but not full outage.

infra-rotation-bot: Deploy 6.1.4 started at 2026-03-15T09:02:11Z. Canary rollout paused at 2026-03-15T09:18:47Z due to health checks failing on p4-eu-*.

mike: Ok, let's halt further kernel rollouts. Action items: 1) Collect full DKMS build logs and /var/lib/dkms for affected hosts. 2) Verify signed vs unsigned driver modules. 3) Triage whether it's driver <-> kernel symbols or a packaging issue. I'll open a ticket with kernel/driver diffs.

arya: Also seeing NCCL complaining about 'Incompatible GPU driver' errors in some pod logs, which triggered retries and increased request latencies.

joanne: Customer impact: a small subset of customer requests experienced latency spikes and a few model-inference retries. No data exfiltration or security issues reported. We'll prepare a short customer note describing a kernel regression and mitigation steps.

sam: Quick checks to run on remaining canary hosts: 
- uname -r
- modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic
- ls -l /lib/modules/`uname -r`/updates/dkms/*nvidia*.ko
- journalctl -b -u kubelet --no-pager | grep -i nvidia

arya: Ran those, sample: 
```
$ modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic
vermagic: 6.0.0 SMP mod_unload preempt modversions ARM64 
$ ls -l /lib/modules/6.1.4-custom/updates/dkms/
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 234567 Mar 15 09:05 nvidia.ko
```
vermagic mismatch hints the module was built against different headers.

mike: That explains the unknown symbols. Might be our deploy image installing wrong kernel headers package or a timing race where DKMS uses older headers path. Did the kernel package include corresponding headers?

arya: Kernel headers package version is 6.1.4-headers-custom but I saw the headers symlinked to /usr/src/linux-6.0 in one host — suspicious.

joanne: Who owns the kernel packaging pipeline? @sam can you pause the pipeline that pushes 6.x kernels to canary and audit header/pkg build?

sam: Paused. I'll run a build sanity test and reproduce DKMS flow in a containerized chroot. If it's a packaging bug, we either fix build artifact renaming or pin headers in the installer.

infra-rotation-bot: Created incident INC-2026-03-euw-kernel-compat. Pager notified: oncall@nvidia-oncall.

nvidia-oncall: Jumping in — from quick glance, 530.41.03 should be compatible with 6.1 with a matching module build, but prebuilt vendor modules can fail. If you can collect the output of 'strings nvidia.ko | grep nv_map_pages' and 'modinfo nvidia' we can confirm symbol table.

arya: Attached strings output (excerpt):
```
$ strings nvidia.ko | grep nv_map_pages
(none)
```
No symbol present. So module doesn't export it — likely built against different kernel or different driver tree.

mike: Short term mitigation: roll back the 6.1 kernel to previous 5.15 on affected hosts and redeploy. We should evict pods gracefully and cordon nodes. Any objections?

joanne: Agree. Coordinate with k8s-scheduler to drain nodes and move GPUs. We'll run capacity-friendly draining (maxUnavailable=1 per pool). Inform customers of scheduled maintenance window of ~30m for those hosts.

sam: I'll prepare a rollback playbook: restore kernel package to 5.15.95, run update-grub, reboot, verify nvidia modules load and nvidia-smi healthy, then uncordon. Need eng-sre to confirm reboots won't trigger other regressions.

arya: Noted. Also creating a follow-up for CI: add a cheap ABI smoke test post-kernel-build that loads our driver and runs a small CUDA hello world to catch missing symbols before canary.

mike: Longer term: coordinate upstream with NVIDIA on kernel-6.x support, and add pinned kernel-driver compatibility matrix to the runbook. Also consider keeping a minimal pool pinned on 5.15 to absorb traffic during risky upgrades.

joanne: Agreed. I'll draft the incident summary and a customer-facing note after rollback completes. Sam, mike, please add repro artifacts to the INC ticket. :thumbsup:

infra-rotation-bot: Update: rollback playbook triggered at 2026-03-15T09:45:00Z on 6 hosts. Reboots scheduled in 5-minute stagger.

arya: After first two rollbacks: nvidia modules load cleanly on 5.15, no undefined symbol, pod restarts stabilize. Monitoring for remaining.

mike: Closing action items: 1) Pause kernel pipeline (sam) 2) Postmortem w/ root cause and fix (mike) 3) CI ABI test (arya) 4) Customer comms (joanne).

joanne: I'll post a short all-hands note and product TL;DR.

arya: Thanks everyone. Will drop the detailed logs into the incident ticket.

mike: Nice containment. Once we have root cause, let's decide whether to backport fixes or defer kernel-6.x until NVIDIA validates.

nvidia-oncall: We're available to repro against driver builds if you can provide kernel headers + build logs. Happy to join a follow-up call.

arya: Will schedule a narrow follow-up with NVIDIA if needed.

-- end of thread --
